You are a weight-space programmer. You read and write the weights of a neural network directly,
by reasoning about what each part of the network computes or should compute.

Rules:
- No gradient descent, no training loops, no fitting weights to data (no least squares on activations,
  no optimizers, no search over random perturbations). Derive every edit from your understanding of the
  network.
- Do not run the network or any of its layers on inputs inside the Python sandbox, even on made-up inputs.
  Static analysis of the weights (norms, SVD, products of weight matrices, comparisons between tensors)
  is fine. The only way to see the network's behaviour is the forward_* tools, which spend a limited budget.
- Prefer small, targeted edits that fix the cause and leave the rest of the network intact.
- When you are done, call `submit` exactly once with your answer and a confidence between 0 and 1.

Task type: FIX. Find the cause of the described failure in the weights, explain it, and fix only that cause by editing weights. Use checkpoints so you can roll back an edit that does not help.

## Task
IMPROVE (fix-style, budgeted). Reduce the network's error, starting with its largest component, without making any region
worse. Measured facts (see the context, "Where the error is"): the biggest error is in deep planned cells (envelope more
than 0.6 m below terrain), RMS 27-30 cm with almost no mean bias, i.e. a shape/placement error of the deep cut, largest on
stalled bites because they are deeper; the region past the predicted stop is only 4-5% of stalled-bite error. Do not
assume the cause: confirm it with the probes (`error_report` now also reports deep_planned / shallow_planned /
beyond_stop; `path_profile`, `error_map`, `compare_groups`, `feature_maps`), then explain it inside the weights.

This copy has two function-preserving additions (predictions are exactly the original network's):
1. Input channel 7 = "beyond the predicted stop" from the hand-written stop calculator (see the context), wired to
   nothing yet (e1.0.weight[:, 7] is zero). Use it if it helps.
2. One spare GroupNorm group per block (listed at the end of the context), all-zero, for new paths, so you need not take
   over channels the network already uses.

Build the smallest edit that fixes a cause you have confirmed. Check every region and both stalled and completed bites
after each change (the judge rejects an edit that makes any region or bite class worse by more than 2 mm on the
validation set, or that does not improve the overall error by more than 2 mm).

Report: which weights you changed, what each change does, and the practice error before and after (all, cut, slump, far,
stalled, completed, deep_planned, shallow_planned, beyond_stop). Restore your best checkpoint before submitting; if
nothing helps, submit the original.


## Context
# The network you are working on

A per-scoop soil model for an autonomous excavator. One forward pass predicts what one bucket scoop does to the ground.
It was trained (gradient descent) to imitate a validated 3D material-point-method (MPM) soil simulator (the "teacher").

Architecture (PyTorch; exact widths, parameter count and spare channels of THIS copy are listed at the end):
- Encoder: e1, e2, e3, e4. Each block: Conv3x3 (.0), GroupNorm (.1), SiLU, Conv3x3 (.3), GroupNorm (.4), SiLU.
  Max-pool 2x2 between blocks. Base widths 32, 64, 128, 256; GroupNorm with 8 groups of equal size.
- Bottleneck head: concat(spatial mean, spatial max) of e4 -> Linear 128 -> SiLU -> Linear 3 = scalars
  [carried bank volume m^3, completion fraction of the planned path, peak actuator demand (x rated force)].
- Decoder: d3 (cat(up e4, e3)), d2 (cat(up d3, e2)), d1 (cat(up d2, e1)), out Conv1x1 -> residual surface change (m)
  per cell. Final prediction = prior (input channel 3) + residual. Every decoder conv sees only a 3x3 neighbourhood.
Grid: the bite's bed, 5 cm cells, 108 x 80 (axis 0 = x, along the drag; axis 1 = y, across the bucket, centred at
y = 40, bucket about 18 cells wide). The bucket usually moves toward DECREASING x (69 of 79 practice bites), but some
bites run toward increasing x; `list_bites` gives each bite's direction.
Input channels:
  0 terrain height minus the mean height under the swept area (m)
  1 swept envelope: lowest bucket point minus terrain over the WHOLE planned path, clipped to [-1.5, 0.5]; 0.5 where the
    bucket never passes
  2 1 where the bucket never passes, else 0
  3 physics prior: cut everything above the planned envelope; if that exceeds the bucket capacity (0.95 m^3) the cut is
    scaled down UNIFORMLY along the whole path (it does not stop part-way); then slopes relax to the friction angle (m)
  4 (friction angle - 30 deg) / 10     5 log10(1 + cohesion Pa) / 3     6 (density - 1800) / 200   (constant planes)
  7 (only in copies that have 8 inputs) beyond the predicted stop: 1 on cells the bucket would first reach after the stop
    calculator's predicted stop point, ramping 0->1 over 5% of the path; 0 on cells reached before it and on untouched
    cells. All-zero on bites the calculator predicts will complete.

The stop calculator (hand-written, uses only terrain, planned poses and soil; fitted on the training tier only): walk the
planned poses in time order; stop at the first pose where the soil the bucket would have had to remove so far exceeds
2.75 m^3, or the passive-wedge digging force at the lip exceeds 43 kN per metre of width. On held-out bites it calls
stall vs complete correctly 90.7% of the time (27 of 108 stall) and, on stalled bites, places the stop within a median
1.0% of the path (assuming no stall gives 31%). It is not perfect: some stalls are missed and a few completed bites
are flagged.

Known physics:
- Passive-wedge (fundamental earthmoving equation) resistance per metre of width at depth d:
  F = 0.5 rho g d^2 Kp + 2 c d sqrt(Kp), Kp = tan^2(45 deg + phi/2). When the machine stalls the bucket stops part-way
  (completion < 1); in front of a stalled bucket the teacher often leaves a pile (+0.3 to +0.7 m), not a cut.
- A cut face of height H and angle beta stands if H <= 4 c sin(beta) cos(phi) / (gamma (1 - cos(beta - phi))) (Culmann);
  otherwise it slumps toward the trench floor.
- Volume: in the teacher, ground lost ~= carried + soil riding on the bucket; nothing is created.

Where the error is (measured on held-out stalled bites the calculator flags; practice is similar): 60-67% of their
squared error is in cells the bucket actually dug before the stop (RMS 19-22 cm), 28-37% outside the path (slumps and
piles, 8-10 cm), only 4-5% past the predicted stop (15-18 cm; there the teacher still shows a cut of about 0.2-0.3 m on
average, roughly 70-95% of the prior's). Within the dug zone the worst cells are where the planned envelope is more than
0.6 m deep: RMS 27-30 cm with almost no mean bias (pred - true about -0.03 to +0.03 m), on stalled AND completed bites.
So the network moves about the right amount of soil but misplaces the deep cut's shape (where the floor, walls and edges
end up). Stalled bites score worse mainly because they contain more deep cells.

This network on the PRACTICE tier (the probes' own metric, RMS over disturbed cells): all 11.8 cm; cut cells 20.9,
slump zone 12.9, far 7.5; stalled bites 13.3 vs completed 10.8; 28 of 79 practice bites stall. The teacher's own
bite-to-bite noise is about 2.3 cm.

What earlier editing sessions on this network found (use it, but check it):
- Taking over channels the network already uses costs more than any fix gains (completed-bite error rose ~0.7-1 cm per
  hijacked group). Build new paths only in spare channels, if this copy has them.
- Envelope depth alone does not separate stalls from completions; the stall is mostly a fill/force effect along the path.
- Earlier tasks assumed stalled-bite error comes from predicting the cut past the stop point. Measurement says otherwise
  (see "Where the error is" below); edits that cancelled the cut past the stop made things worse.
- To pass a signal through GroupNorm predictably, keep the group's statistics fixed (e.g. a large constant channel plus
  zero-sum channels), or work in a spare group whose other channels are zero.

Tools: `python` runs code with R (read-only weights) and W (writable); use checkpoint(label) to save good versions and
restore the best one before you submit: the weights you submit are what is judged. Probes run the network on PRACTICE
bites only and cost forward passes (list_bites is free).

Rules: do not train or fit weights to data with an optimizer, and do not run the network except through the probes (a
separate validation set and two full trenches you never see decide whether your edit is kept). Prefer small, explainable
edits; say what each edit should change, so it can be checked.

## This copy: 2,542,728 weights, 8 input channels (channel 7 = beyond the predicted stop)
- e1: in 8, out 36, GroupNorm 9 groups of 4
- e2: in 36, out 72, GroupNorm 9 groups of 8
- e3: in 72, out 144, GroupNorm 9 groups of 16
- e4: in 144, out 288, GroupNorm 9 groups of 32
- d3: in 432, out 144, GroupNorm 9 groups of 16
- d2: in 216, out 72, GroupNorm 9 groups of 8
- d1: in 108, out 36, GroupNorm 9 groups of 4
- SPARE: each block has one extra GroupNorm group appended after its original channels (e1/d1 32-35, e2/d2 64-71, e3/d3 128-143, e4 256-287). All weights into and out of spare channels are exactly zero, so they output 0 and the predictions equal the original network's. Concatenated decoder inputs keep each source's spare channels right after its originals (d1.0 input: d2 0-63, spare 64-71, e1 72-103, spare 104-107; d2.0: d3 0-127, spare 128-143, e2 144-207, spare 208-215; d3.0: e4 0-255, spare 256-287, e3 288-415, spare 416-431); out.weight inputs 32-35 are spare; head.0 input = [e4 mean 0-287 | e4 max 288-575].
- Input channel 7 enters only e1.0; e1.0.weight[:, 7] is all zero, so the network currently ignores it.

## Forward passes (budget 50)

completion (<0.9 = the machine stalled), the stop calculator's predicted completion (what input channel 7 encodes,
when present), drag direction along x, and grid size.
  forward_error_report (cost 1): RMS surface error (m) on the practice tier: all, by region (cut / slump within 0.5 m / far), stalled vs completed
bites, by planned depth (deep_planned: envelope more than 0.6 m below terrain; shallow_planned), beyond_stop (cells
channel 7 marks), and carried-volume error (m^3).
  forward_worst_bites (cost 1): The k practice bites with the largest RMS error: name, rmse, completion (<0.9 = the machine stalled), soil.
  forward_path_profile (cost 1): One practice bite, row by row along x (every `step` rows), averaged over the bucket width (y = 31..49):
true change, predicted change, prior (ch 3), envelope (ch 1), beyond-stop (ch 7 if present) and terrain (ch 0).
Also the true / predicted completion and drag direction. The quickest way to see where a stalled bite stopped.
  forward_error_map (cost 1): One practice bite as 2-D maps (m), coarse stride chosen to fit. fields: any of terrain_rel, true_change,
pred_change, error, prior, beyond_stop (comma separated).
  forward_feature_maps (cost 1): Activations of a named module (e.g. 'e4', 'd1', 'e1.3') on one practice bite: mean and max of EVERY channel, plus
coarse maps of the listed channels (comma separated, e.g. '1,17,33'; default first 4). Outputs NOT returned.
  forward_compare_groups (cost 1): One layer over ALL practice bites: per channel, mean of the spatial mean and of the spatial max on stalled vs
completed bites, ranked by the standardised gap in the max. Shows which channels carry stall information.

I found no edit that clears the judge's bar, so I am submitting the ORIGINAL weights. diff() shows nothing changed.

Practice error, original network (RMS in m; this is also "after", since nothing changed): all 0.1178, cut 0.2091, slump 0.1289, far 0.0755, stalled 0.1335, completed 0.1077, deep_planned 0.2990, shallow_planned 0.1357, beyond_stop 0.1799, carried MAE 0.079 m^3.

**What I checked in the weights.** I looked at every tensor: norms, per-channel input and output norms, how the 3×3 weights spread over kernel positions (including the decoder skip blocks), GroupNorm parameters, and the out layer. Nothing looks corrupted: no flipped or shifted kernels, no dead or scaled channels, no odd GroupNorm parameters. The spare channels and e1.0.weight[:,7] are all zero, as stated. The deep-cut error is not a single broken weight.

**What the probes show** (path profiles and maps of 15 bites, worst-bite list, compare_groups on e4):
1. **Bites dragged toward +x (all saturated silt).** The network has no input that tells it the drag direction. It has learned the rule for the 87% of bites dragged toward −x: the low-x end of a cut is the end of the path, where a full bucket rides over the trench and leaves a shallow cut.
   - On completed +x bites (0099, 0102, 0079) the truth is a deep cut of about 0.6–0.9 × the envelope at the low-x start. The network predicts roughly the prior or less, about 0.4–0.5 m too shallow.
   - On +x stalls the calculator missed (0087, 0089, 0093), the truth is about 0 at that same start.
   - Nothing in the inputs separates these two groups, so the network predicts a value between them. That fits deep-cell error with large RMS and almost no mean bias.
2. **Stalls the calculator flags.** The network already knows these are stalls: its completion head is within a few percent, and many e4 channels fire much higher on stalled bites. Before the stop the deep floor is mostly right. The leftover error is at the stop edge: the network's deep cut runs about 3–6 cells past the calculator's stop, cutting 0.3–0.7 m too deep where channel 7 is just starting to ramp up (0091, 0097, 0081, 0009; 0072 is the opposite). Further past the stop it cuts too little.
3. **c140-wet-clay_0009** is about 11% of all squared error on its own. The calculator puts the stop at 0.715 against a true 0.62. The network predicts a −1.3 m blob over terrain pits where the envelope is only about −0.24 m and the truth is a pile in front of the stalled bucket.

**Edit I tried and reverted.** I wired channel 7 into the input layer: e1.0.weight[:,7] = 2·w[:,1] + 1·w[:,2]. This tells the network "the bucket never reached the cells past the stop". It made things much worse: all 0.1403, stalled 0.1831, deep_planned 0.446, beyond_stop 0.375, cut 0.282; completed unchanged at 0.1077. I restored the original.

**Why I did not build a spare-channel path.** Each candidate was estimated from the error numbers and probe profiles; none was built or measured:
- **Channel-7 correction near the stop.** Channel 7 helps only on flagged stalls. From the error report I estimate stalled bites hold about 47% of the squared error and the region past the stop about 2% of the total. Even sharpening the stop edge well should gain under 1 mm, short of the required 2 mm.
- **+x direction detector.** One could be built from where the cut runs off the grid, using spare channels, but it would deepen the start of the missed +x stalls too and push the stalled class past the 2 mm limit.
- **Capping the cut at the envelope** (which would fix 0009) would need the network's own output inside a nonlinearity, and the 1×1 out layer has none after it.

**Conclusion.** The deep-cut shape error comes from missing information: drag direction, whether the bucket stalled when the calculator misses it, and the stop position at full resolution. No weight is broken. The only extra input, channel 7, can't recover enough of the error to clear the bar.

**Edit I tried and reverted.** I wired channel 7 into the input layer: e1.0.weight[:,7] = 2·w[:,1] + 1·w[:,2]. This tells the network "the bucket never reached the cells past the stop". It made things much worse: all 0.1403, stalled 0.1831, deep_planned 0.446, beyond_stop 0.375, cut 0.282; completed unchanged at 0.1077. I restored the original.

**Why I did not build a spare-channel path.** Each candidate was estimated from the error numbers and probe profiles; none was built or measured:
- **Channel-7 correction near the stop.** Channel 7 helps only on flagged stalls. From the error report I estimate stalled bites hold about 47% of the squared error and the region past the stop about 2% of the total. Even sharpening the stop edge well should gain under 1 mm, short of the required 2 mm.
- **+x direction detector.** One could be built from where the cut runs off the grid, using spare channels, but it would deepen the start of the missed +x stalls too and push the stalled class past the 2 mm limit.
- **Capping the cut at the envelope** (which would fix 0009) would need the network's own output inside a nonlinearity, and the 1×1 out layer has none after it.

**Conclusion.** The deep-cut shape error comes from missing information: drag direction, whether the bucket stalled when the calculator misses it, and the stop position at full resolution. No weight is broken. The only extra input, channel 7, can't recover enough of the error to clear the bar.
